nodes.title: SG-1.2 Write pure grid-to-pixels and sprite-sheet functions
nodes.body:
Context: game/frontend/src/lib/palette.ts exports PALETTE, a 48-entry list of '#rrggbb' strings. No art code exists yet. Desired behaviour: pure, deterministic functions convert a palette-indexed grid to RGBA bytes and arrange frames into a sheet. Expected result: unit tests check width, height, frame count, palette-only colours and that an out-of-range index throws. Why: SG-1.3 builds the PNG script on top of these functions.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a grid of palette indices, when gridToRgba runs, then it returns RGBA bytes of width*height*4 whose colours all come from PALETTE.
- Given an index outside the palette, when gridToRgba runs, then it throws.
- Given N equal-size frames, when buildSpriteSheet runs, then width, height and frameCount describe the sheet and every pixel colour is in PALETTE.


## Scope
- In scope: New pure modules under game/frontend/src/art
- In scope: Unit tests in game/frontend/tests
- Out of scope: PNG writing script and manifest update (SG-1.3)
- Out of scope: Authoring sprite grids
- Out of scope: New rooms, story content, backend, audio, deployment, repository clean-up
- Preserve: game/frontend/src/lib/palette.ts exports and its tests
- Preserve: Phaser ~3.90.0 pin
- Preserve: Go API contracts


## Technical constraints
- Phaser stays on 3.90.x; React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind, Radix, Zustand stay.
- Shared palette of at most 48 colours defined once in src/lib/palette.ts; reuse it, do not redefine colours.
- All art is generated in-repo and deterministically; no downloaded art or CDN.
- Tests are unit tests with all dependencies mocked.


## Definition of done
- Both requirements are met and their Verify units pass.


## Non-functional requirements
- Functions are pure and deterministic: identical input gives identical bytes.


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · gridToRgba converts a palette-indexed grid to RGBA and rejects bad indices
nodes.body:
Context: palette colours are hex strings in PALETTE. Desired behaviour: gridToRgba(grid) returns width, height and a Uint8ClampedArray of RGBA. Index -1 means transparent (alpha 0); any other index outside 0..PALETTE.length-1, or a non-integer, throws a RangeError; rows of unequal length throw. Expected result: every opaque pixel equals a PALETTE colour. Why: guarantees art uses only the shared palette.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a 3x2 grid, when converted, then width is 3, height is 2 and data length is 24.
- Given any valid grid, when converted, then each opaque pixel's rgb matches the hex of PALETTE[index] with alpha 255.
- Given index 48, -2 or 1.5, when converted, then a RangeError is thrown.
- Given the same grid twice, when converted, then the byte arrays are equal.


## Scope
- In scope: gridToRgba and a hex-to-rgb helper
- Out of scope: Sheet layout
- Out of scope: PNG encoding
- Preserve: PALETTE definition


## Technical constraints
- Palette of at most 48 colours, defined once and reused.
- Pure function, no I/O.


## Dependencies
- INT


## Definition of done
- gridToRgba is exported from game/frontend/src/art/pixelGrid.ts.


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · buildSpriteSheet lays equal-size frames into one horizontal sheet with size and frame metadata
nodes.body:
Context: sprites are animation frames, each a palette-indexed grid. Desired behaviour: buildSpriteSheet(frames) validates that frames is non-empty and all share width and height (else throws Error), converts each with gridToRgba and places them left to right. Returns { width: frameWidth*count, height: frameHeight, frameWidth, frameHeight, frameCount, data }. Expected result: sheet metadata matches what SG-1.3 will write into the manifest. Why: manifest needs real size, frame size and frame count.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given 4 frames of 32x48, when built, then width 128, height 48, frameWidth 32, frameHeight 48, frameCount 4.
- Given frame k, when read at x offset k*frameWidth, then its pixels equal gridToRgba of that frame.
- Given an empty list or frames of different sizes, when built, then it throws.
- Given a frame with an out-of-range index, when built, then it throws.


## Scope
- In scope: buildSpriteSheet
- Out of scope: PNG encoding
- Out of scope: manifest writing
- Preserve: gridToRgba behaviour


## Technical constraints
- Pure function, deterministic output.
- Palette of at most 48 colours defined once.


## Dependencies
- REQ1


## Definition of done
- buildSpriteSheet is exported from game/frontend/src/art/spriteSheet.ts.


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.description: Create the pure module converting a palette-indexed grid into RGBA bytes using PALETTE from src/lib/palette.ts.
acceptance_criteria: gridToRgba returns width, height and RGBA data for valid grids.
Out-of-range or non-integer indices throw RangeError.
technical_constraints: Reuse PALETTE; do not redefine colours (shared palette, max 48).
definition_of_done: Module compiles under tsc --noEmit and exports PixelGrid, TRANSPARENT and gridToRgba.

steps.action: Create the file importing PALETTE from '../lib/palette'. Export type PixelGrid = readonly (readonly number[])[], export const TRANSPARENT = -1, and a local hexToRgb(hex) returning [r,g,b] parsed from the 6 hex digits after '#'.
steps.expected: File compiles with the three declarations.

steps.action: Export gridToRgba(grid: PixelGrid): { width: number; height: number; data: Uint8ClampedArray }. height = grid.length, width = grid[0]?.length ?? 0. Throw Error if any row length differs from width. Allocate Uint8ClampedArray(width*height*4). For each cell: if value === TRANSPARENT leave zeros; else if !Number.isInteger(value) or value<0 or value>=PALETTE.length throw RangeError with the value, x and y; else write hexToRgb(PALETTE[value]) and alpha 255 at offset (y*width+x)*4.
steps.code: export function gridToRgba(grid: PixelGrid) { /* as described */ }
steps.expected: gridToRgba([[0,1],[2,-1]]) returns width 2, height 2, 16 bytes with the last pixel alpha 0.

steps.action: Create the file importing gridToRgba and PixelGrid from './pixelGrid'. Export interface SpriteSheet { width: number; height: number; frameWidth: number; frameHeight: number; frameCount: number; data: Uint8ClampedArray }.

Export buildSpriteSheet(frames: readonly PixelGrid[]): SpriteSheet. Throw Error('no frames') when frames.length is 0. Convert every frame with gridToRgba; throw Error if any width/height differs from the first frame's. Set sheetWidth = frameWidth*frames.length. Allocate Uint8ClampedArray(sheetWidth*frameHeight*4). For frame k and row y, data.set(frameData.subarray(y*frameWidth*4,(y+1)*frameWidth*4), (y*sheetWidth + k*frameWidth)*4). Return the metadata and data.
steps.code: export function buildSpriteSheet(frames: readonly PixelGrid[]): SpriteSheet { /* as described */ }
steps.expected: 4 frames of 32x48 give width 128, height 48, frameCount 4.
